findings.passage: As you may or may not know, it was the Republican majority that provided an opportunity through the mail in ballot system to let people have another opportunity on how to vote, which happened to be very timely with the COVID situation. Through the primary, we saw there were some problems when some counties chose to take it upon themselves and do more than what the state statute allows, as far as providing drop boxes, which were not necessarily monitored.
findings.note: Interview transcript (WPSU, answering how he works to keep voting secure). He describes the mail-in ballot system and criticises county drop boxes that went beyond state law.

findings.passage: We should all want safe, secure election process so that your vote isn't canceled out by somebody who came by 24 hours, 48 hours later and tried to change the outcome.
findings.note: Same interview. He objects to counting mail ballots with no postmark that arrive days after election day. Nothing on voter ID.

findings.passage: I am alarmed and incredibly concerned about the numerous process failures, mistakes and reports of misdeeds in the 2020 election.
findings.note: Statement in his name (as House Majority Leader) in a caucus release about letters to Congress, the attorney general and the inspector general on the 2020 election. Nothing on voter ID.
